subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and goal mode as core runtime features now, and should the linked implementation land as one branch or be split?
rationale: The request adds cross-surface core behavior, protocol/API surfaces, UI/channel rendering, and goal-continuation semantics, so the remaining choice is product and ownership direction rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Split staged PRs
options.body: Review question infrastructure, plan mode, and goal mode as separate staged changes with focused proof for each surface.

options.title: Sponsor full branch
options.body: Accept the broad review cost and drive the linked implementation branch through proof, rebase, and security review as one feature.

options.title: Defer or narrow
options.body: Keep only the smaller existing primitives for now and reopen specific core/plugin API gaps when maintainers want each capability.

recommendation.title: Split staged PRs
recommendation.body: Review question infrastructure, plan mode, and goal mode as separate staged changes with focused proof for each surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The plan-tool and strict-agentic history makes this the best available routing owner for the core runtime direction decision.
